listenings.text: Hi, I'm Tom, and I'm a recruiter in Miami. I find people for companies in the United States and in Latin America. Last year I worked on a job for an HR director in Brazil. The posting asked for fluent English. We got about two hundred applications, but many of the best people didn't apply. I called some of them later. They all said the same thing: I didn't think my English was good enough. In the end, we hired a woman with very good experience and clear, simple English. Her English was not perfect, and that was not a problem. So my advice is: read the requirements, but don't give up before the deadline.

My name is Sophie. Three years ago I saw a job in Edinburgh, in Scotland. It was my dream job, but it asked for experience with international teams, and I didn't have much. I wrote my application on a Sunday, and then I didn't send it. On Monday I read it again. On Tuesday, the last day, I sent it at eleven at night, one hour before the deadline. A week later, a recruiter called me. I was so nervous that I forgot my own phone number! I didn't get that job. But the recruiter remembered me, and two months later she offered me a better one.

reading.rtitle: The Job I Didn’t Apply For
paras: Two years ago, on a Monday morning, I saw a job posting on a professional network. An international company wanted an HR director for Latin America. I read the posting three times. I had the experience, I knew the work, and I really wanted the job. But one requirement was in bold: fluent English. I closed the page.

The deadline was Friday. Every day that week, I opened the posting again, and every day I thought: my English is not good enough. On Friday night, the posting was still on my screen, but I didn’t apply. Later, a friend from that company told me something difficult: the person they hired didn’t speak perfect English either.

That was the moment I decided not to give up. I started English classes the next month. It was not easy, and I didn’t have much time, but I studied in the car, at lunch and on weekends. Last month, a recruiter called me about a similar job. This time I sent my CV. Did I get the job? I don’t know yet. But I got an interview, and I got a second chance. — Marina, HR director
